resources.string: Grant Android Modify system settings once, then enable Display control for this tablet in Home Assistant. Brightness only; it cannot physically turn the screen off or wake a locked device.
Audio, voice and camera. Connected to your home.
Connect Home Assistant once, then choose the features you need.
Pair your Echo in Android’s Bluetooth settings and enable media audio. Test music playback on the tablet first.
Keep this device and Home Assistant on the same local network. Select a discovered address or enter your own.
Use the base address only, without /lovelace, /dashboard or other paths.
Looking for Home Assistant on your network…
Found Home Assistant. Tap an address to use it.
Search complete. Select an address or enter one manually.
Search paused. Tap Find Home Assistant to try again.
No server found. Check the Wi-Fi network and HA Zeroconf, or enter the address manually. Guest networks may block discovery.
Network discovery is unavailable. Check Wi-Fi or enter the address manually.
Could not start the search. Check Wi-Fi and try again.
Address selected. Add your token, then start the player.
Address selected. Review the HTTP option before starting.
Allow unencrypted HTTP for this local address
With HTTP, your token, audio and enabled camera images travel unencrypted on the local network. This permission applies only to the address and port shown above.
In Home Assistant: Profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens → Create token. Name it TAFA Device Bridge, then select Generate QR code in the creation dialog.
The token and its QR code are shown only when you create it. Scan before closing the dialog. If it is already closed, create a new token.
A token is saved. Leave this field empty to keep it.
Stored encrypted when you start the player. The optional wakeword service uses the microphone only after you start it.
Complete the setup, then start the player.
Checking Home Assistant and the Bluetooth output.
Return to your Echo Relay dashboard in Home Assistant and start a voice request. Keep this player running.
Building a small audio buffer. MP3 and PCM/WAV can play while the remaining audio is still arriving.
The actual Bluetooth output has been confirmed.
The player is waiting for the next answer.
Home Assistant is connected, but no Bluetooth media output is available.
Check the HA address, Wi-Fi and token. Open Diagnostics for the latest status.
Android could not confirm the Bluetooth output. Check that the Echo is connected for media audio, then retry.
Check the saved address, token and HTTP permission, then start the player again.
Player and keepalive are under Settings → Echo & audio player.

While the player runs, a silent local audio loop keeps Bluetooth media active. Can reduce Echo’s “Playing from…” announcements, but is not guaranteed. Automatically retries if Bluetooth drops. May affect Alexa music or battery usage.
Use either this keepalive or the HA dashboard keepalive. Turn it off if normal Alexa playback is affected.
Keepalive unavailable · turn off and back on to retry

1. Open Connect, select Home Assistant and scan the one-time token QR code from your HA profile.

2. Pair your Bluetooth speaker and test media playback in Android.

3. Start the player for audio output, or open Wakeword for optional local microphone recognition. Camera settings are available from Status.

4. Return to your compatible TAFA dashboard for voice requests. Keep the relevant Android service notification active.

TAFA Device Bridge uses the existing Echo Relay audio integration. The matching HA backend and dashboard must be installed separately. Each tablet keeps its own device ID for multiroom wakeword settings.

The prompt is generated by the Echo itself. Keepalive can reduce idle gaps but cannot guarantee that Echo announcements are suppressed. Stopping the player also stops its keepalive. Nothing starts automatically after a reboot.
If Android stops the player while idle, check this app’s battery settings and allow background activity if needed. Keep the tablet powered for continuous operation.
This stops the player and removes the saved server address, HTTP permission and encrypted token. To revoke the token itself, delete it in your HA profile.
Scan or enter a token before starting.
The address changed. Scan or enter a token for this server.
Enter a base HA address without a path, username or URL parameters.
HTTP is only allowed for local IP addresses. Use network discovery or HTTPS.
Explicitly allow HTTP for this local address, or use HTTPS.
This QR code does not contain a plain HA access token. Scan the code from the token creation dialog.
Setup could not be completed. Check the address and token, then try again.
No camera is available. Paste or enter the token instead.
Scan the HA token QR code · Back to cancel
Camera access is needed to scan this token. You can also paste it manually.
Share the front or rear camera with HA, optionally report image movement, or run a local camera test.
Choose a camera, then tap Start. Access is requested only then. Preview and test images stay on this screen; leaving it switches the camera off and clears the image.
No test image. Images are kept only in memory.
Test image from %1$s · %2$d × %3$d · on this device only

In HA, use camera.echo_relay_tablet for images and Jarvis Tablet Audio: Describe camera for the local vision model. Select your outdoor/door camera in the integration options. Image movement is a simple pixel comparison and can react to lighting; it does not recognize people or objects. Continuous capture needs power and may need Android battery settings adjusted. Nothing starts automatically after a reboot.
No camera is available on this device.
Camera could not be used. Another app may be using it, or this device may not support the preview. Stop other camera apps and try again.
Camera access was not granted. You can allow it in Android app settings and tap Start again. Audio works without camera access.
Scan cancelled. Your existing token was not changed.
Token scanned. Start the player to save it encrypted.
Bluetooth audio bridge · tap to open

Send JPEG snapshots to your TAFA room using the saved HA room-user login. First enable Camera for the room under Apps → TAFA → Devices & multiroom. Start explicitly and stop here or via the notification. No recording or separate Jarvis receiver required.
HA camera active · images are arriving
Save your HA address and token in audio setup first. Camera access does not require a running audio player.
Image delivery interrupted · retrying. Check Wi-Fi and HA. Old images expire in HA after 15 seconds.
Camera access denied. Enable the camera for this room under Apps → TAFA → Devices & multiroom and use the HA token for that room user. No admin token is needed.
TAFA camera endpoint not found. Update the TAFA integration on this HA server and restart Home Assistant Core. No separate Jarvis receiver is needed.
Another tablet is already streaming to this TAFA room. Stop its camera stream before starting this one.
Camera image could not be prepared. Stop and restart the HA camera.
Camera active · sending images to Home Assistant
TAFA uses one audio path: microphone → Home Assistant → this tablet → Bluetooth. Pair a room once in TAFA Dashboard → TAFA → Devices.
Stored on this tablet. Changes apply during the next capture cycle. Actual delivery may be slower depending on capture, upload and server load.
Wakeword detection works even with the tablet screen off. After the wakeword, speech goes directly to Home Assistant. Set the local follow-up limit under Settings → Native Assist.

Optional German model (~45 MB). Download it once on this device. Recognition audio stays local. Turn off the dashboard’s own wakeword detector before using native recognition; Alexa may also trigger an Echo.
Allow microphone access to test wakeword recognition.
This is a hypothesis-confirmation count, NOT an audio volume or decibel threshold. 1 = more sensitive, 3 = fewer false activations but possible missed calls.
Settings are synchronized per device with Home Assistant. Muting releases the Android microphone while the service stays running. Changes take effect after the next sync.
Could not save wakeword settings to Home Assistant: %1$s
Unlimited tablets: each installation gets a unique random ID. Enter a room name, start native recognition and select/pair the tablet in TAFA under Voice & Audio. No numbered slot restrictions.
Optional local recognition. You choose when the microphone is active.
Setup guidance, background operation and connection details.
Recognize a wakeword on this device and let your TAFA dashboard handle the question.
Only using wakeword recognition? Switch to Wakeword and start it there; the same connection is saved.
Live status of the audio service. Useful when troubleshooting with the project documentation.
Camera use is optional. Local preview and transmission each start only when you request them.
The built-in foreground wakeword service sends questions directly to Home Assistant Assist. Replies return to this tablet and play over Bluetooth. No dashboard window is required.
Follow-up questions are configured per device in Home Assistant
Start the Bluetooth player, pair this tablet with an HA room and start native wakeword detection.

Speech is sent to your Home Assistant after a wakeword, Speak now or an explicitly enabled follow-up (at most your local limit). It is not stored as a recording. End conversation returns to local wakeword detection. Stop or mute the wakeword service to release the microphone.
Voice, Bluetooth, microphone, display and camera for this tablet.
Connections, voice and camera at a glance. Start common actions here.
Find Home Assistant and set the server address and room-user token.
Pair your Echo in Android, start the TAFA player, then optionally keep Bluetooth media active silently.
Grant permission here. Control brightness and dimming in the TAFA Control Center; this does not reliably power the display on or off.
Send image changes to Home Assistant: motion binary sensor for this TAFA room while fresh images arrive. Not person/object recognition.
Motion sensor: available only while camera is streaming
Motion detection enabled (HA sensor available during camera upload)
Uses your saved Home Assistant connection. Missing details open Connect.

Speak now starts one question without a wakeword. Start wakeword listens locally for the call word. End conversation returns to wakeword detection; mute in Home Assistant or stop the wakeword service to turn the microphone off.
The microphone is muted in Home Assistant. Unmute this device there first.

Default: the wakeword is required again after every answer. Optionally allow 1–10 additional questions per conversation. Silence, an error or this limit returns to wakeword detection. This local ceiling also applies without a dashboard; Home Assistant may reduce it. Background sounds can still be mistaken for speech during an open follow-up window.
